newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's telecommunications staff to stage strike.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's telecommunications staff to stage strike.

text.p: Morocco's 24,000 telecommunications utility staff will go on a one-day strike on June 5 to protest against the upcoming privatisation of the sector and to press for pay increases and other benefits, their union said on Thursday.

"We think that opening up the sector to private operators will not help spread the network to rural areas or improve the social aspects", a spokesman for the union operating under the umbrella of the Democratic Labour Confederation said.
Among their demands are a 10 percent pay increase as agreed by the August accord signed between the government and unions last year.
He said the 640 telecommunications and postal services (ONPT) agencies will provide a minimum service.
Morocco plans to split the ONPT into two enterprises called Ittissalat al-Maghrib and Barid al-Maghrib. Privatisation will first target GSM phones then be extended to the whole network.
Morocco with a population of 27 million people has only four telephone lines per 100 people and 30,000 GSM subscribers.
The spokesman said the draft law has been approved by a parliamentary commission and is expected to be adopted soon but gave no date.
